clue.text: Glen raider going out as head of the gang

indicators.note: going out suggests these words breaking up and leaving their order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A raider from a glen setting off on a foray as the gang's chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' rearranges the ten letters of GLEN RAIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The leader of a gang, especially one stirring up trouble, is its chief instigator.

clue.text: Desiring somehow to get prime position to watch fight

indicators.note: somehow says the word Desiring is turned into another word by some reshuffle of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone longing to get the best seat at a boxing match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the eight letters of DESIRING.
explanation.definitionFit: The area right beside a boxing ring gives spectators the closest view of a bout.

clue.text: One fool in the province meeting another

parts.note: in British usage 'the Province' is Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI
another fool, following on from 'One fool', is a twit

explanation.surface: Two idiots bumping into each other somewhere in the provinces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' borrows 'fool' from the definition: another fool is a TWIT. 'The province' is a standard British name for Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a silly, stupid person.

clue.text: Relations going to the toilet — short visit

indicators.note: the relations going to the toilet are placed after it, so the toilet word comes first

parts.note: loo is British slang for the toilet
kin means family relations

explanation.surface: Family members heading off to the lavatory for a brief call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' means the relations come after the toilet; the surface's comic trip to the lavatory hides a brief call on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To look in on someone is to drop by briefly, a quick call.

clue.text: A research establishment has plant substance that's white

parts.note: a lab, short for laboratory, is a place where research is done
an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A laboratory owns a plant that yields a white material.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a fine white mineral, a form of gypsum used for carving and proverbial for whiteness.

clue.text: Poor woman entertaining senior cleric having abandoned work

indicators.note: entertaining is used in the sense of hosting a guest, so the woman's name holds the other piece within it

parts.note: Ruby is a woman's name

indicators.note: having abandoned says the cleric's title drops the letters for work

parts.note: a bishop is a senior member of the clergy
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A woman hosting a bishop who has walked out of his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having abandoned' drops the work from the senior cleric's title, and 'entertaining' has the woman hold what remains; 'Poor' looks like pity for her but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbishy things are worthless or of low quality, a colloquial word for second-rate.

clue.text: Be convenient for clubs, say

explanation.surface: Whether a card game arrangement fits a player holding clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: To be convenient for someone is to fit their needs; clubs is one of the four card groupings, alongside hearts, diamonds and spades.

clue.text: Earmark time to go into holiday area

indicators.note: to go into means the abbreviation for time is placed inside the holiday word

parts.note: the seaside is the coast as a destination for holidays

explanation.surface: Reserving some time to spend on a trip to the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark something is to reserve it for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Consider as perfect stupid ladies? That is going to extremes!

indicators.note: going to extremes means the letters for that is go at the two ends, around the rest

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: stupid suggests the word ladies is muddled up, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: An exclamation that seeing silly women as flawless is taking things too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' jumbles LADIES into DEALIS; 'going to extremes' puts I and E at either end of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To idealise is to regard something as better than it really is, flawless.

clue.text: Person of the country, one getting on in old sa province

indicators.note: in means the letters for one and on are placed inside the old province's name

parts.note: Natal was a province of South Africa until 1994
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A citizen climbing the ranks in a former South African province.
explanation.walkthrough: Natal, now part of KwaZulu-Natal, was one of the four provinces of the old South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a particular state.

clue.text: Maggot the woman found to give a bit of trouble

parts.note: a bot is the maggot-like larva of the botfly
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A woman discovering a maggot that causes her some trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To bother someone is to annoy or disturb them a little.

clue.text: Sword? I'm getting it — mark left by wound outside

indicators.note: outside means the wound mark goes around the other letters

parts.note: a scar is the mark a healed wound leaves
I'm without its apostrophe gives two letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sword fighter realising they are about to be cut and scarred.
explanation.definitionFit: A scimitar is a curved oriental blade.

clue.text: Be rude to one bridge team ultimately

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
in bridge, North and South play as a partnership, abbreviated NS
ult. is a dictionary abbreviation for ultimately

explanation.surface: Snubbing one of the pairs at a bridge table in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named by compass points, North-South partnering against East-West.
explanation.definitionFit: To insult is to speak or act offensively towards someone.

clue.text: 'That's rubbish, mate!'

explanation.surface: A dismissive retort to a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is British slang for nonsense, and also a jocular British form of address to a man, like pal.

clue.text: A situation in which someone must take stock

definitions.text: A situation in which someone must take stock

parts.words: A situation in which someone must take stock
parts.note: reads as a moment demanding reflection, but means a place where goods are taken and kept

explanation.definitionFit: A room for storing supplies is literally where stock is taken in and held.

clue.text: Ruler's office makes them cross

parts.note: 'em is a colloquial shortening of them
cross in the sense of angry means irate

explanation.surface: An official's room that leaves visitors annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' just links, so the clue reads as "'em irate".
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is the territory or position of an emir, a Muslim ruler.

clue.text: Agent goes to hospital unwell — exaggerators make much of it

indicators.note: goes to says the spy is followed by the letters for hospital

parts.note: a mole is a spy, an agent planted inside an organisation
unwell means ill

explanation.surface: A sick spy checks into hospital and exaggerators make a fuss about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idiom 'make a mountain out of a molehill', to exaggerate a small problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of making a mountain out of a small mound means blowing a trifle up out of proportion.

clue.text: Banter from salesperson with skill and energy repeatedly

parts.note: rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
art means skill

indicators.note: repeatedly here means the letter for energy appears twice

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Witty talk from a skilful, energetic travelling salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick, witty conversation or retorts.

clue.text: Char may be seen at this social event

definitions.text: Char may be seen at this social event

parts.words: Char may be seen at this social event
parts.note: char is a British word for a cleaning lady, but also slang for the hot drink served at this afternoon gathering

explanation.definitionFit: An afternoon dance with refreshments served, popular in the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Sort prepared to be put into print

parts.note: a sort or type is a kind
set means ready, prepared

explanation.surface: A kind of item that is ready for printing.
explanation.definitionFit: To typeset text is to arrange it in type ready for printing.

clue.text: Politician — one allowed to bring in something cosmetic?

indicators.note: to bring in means the politician's word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party
I is the Roman numeral for one
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A politician permitted to introduce a merely cosmetic measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something cosmetic?' looks like political window-dressing; the question mark flags it as a toiletries item.
explanation.definitionFit: A toiletry is a product used in washing or grooming, such as a cream or soap.

clue.text: Thus monster is repelled

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the monster word is read backwards

parts.note: an ogre is a man-eating giant, a monster

explanation.surface: Accordingly, the monster is driven off.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore.

clue.text: Some jackass, ignorant delegate

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An ignorant fool handed responsibility by a manager.
explanation.definitionFit: To delegate a task is to hand it to someone else.

clue.text: A new king, a king coming to a capital city

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
taken as written
R, from Latin rex, stands for king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newly crowned monarch and another king arrive in a nation's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming to' simply joins the last A to the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankara is the capital of Turkey.

clue.text: Fellow gets embarrassed about being put back in clink

indicators.note: about means the embarrassed word goes around the fellow

parts.note: red, as in red-faced, means embarrassed
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man blushes on being sent back to jail.
explanation.definitionFit: To remand an accused person is to return them to custody pending trial.

clue.text: Individual is rude

explanation.surface: Someone who is impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal means belonging to one particular person, and personal remarks are offensively directed at someone.

clue.text: Poet left at illegally high speed going by motorway

indicators.note: going by means placed next to, so the motorway sits beside the other letters

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first major motorway, written MI in crosswords
a ton is slang for a hundred miles per hour, well over the British speed limit

explanation.surface: A poet speeding illegally at a hundred on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 runs from London to Leeds; its 1 is read as the letter I. 'Doing a ton' is British slang for driving at 100 mph.
explanation.definitionFit: John Milton was the English poet of Paradise Lost.

clue.text: Pushy cook, maiden at home, little worker?

parts.note: to do food is to cook it, as in doing the potatoes
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
in means at home
an ant is a small worker insect

explanation.surface: Asking whether a domineering cook, a young woman at home, is merely a lowly worker.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominant people are assertive and like to control others.

clue.text: Bush, dull to listen to

indicators.note: to listen to says the clue word's synonym is heard, and a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: slow can mean dull, as in a slow evening

explanation.surface: A shrub that is boring to hear about.
explanation.walkthrough: SLOW and the entered word are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The blackthorn shrub bears small sour fruit used to flavour gin, and its name is given to the plant itself.

clue.text: Enemy later beaten, this being simple

indicators.note: beaten suggests the words being knocked about and bashed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The foe defeated in due course, which proved easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' rearranges the ten letters of ENEMY LATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary means basic and easy, as in Holmes's famous retort.
